historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly rejects agent execution and remote visual certification, but does not define connection coverage, safe handling, routing/bend-radius rules or physical evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly retains MANUAL ONLY and expands the inspection to match, keying, seating, retention, pins, routing, strain and optional post-power corroboration.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A connected endpoint can enumerate despite partial seating, a damaged pin or excessive cable strain. The authoritative check must trace each source-to-destination cable and connector against the build map, inspecting both ends and the entire routing path before power-on.

original_test_intent: Verify manually that every specified node, component and cable is connected to the correct endpoint, fully seated and retained, undamaged and routed/positioned according to the platform build specification.
original_method: With the SUT isolated and ESD-controlled, use an approved endpoint/routing map to trace every connection end-to-end, inspect keying, pins, seating, latch/fastener, bend radius, support, strain and clearance, photograph both endpoints and route, stop on any mismatch or damage, then leave the assembly in a verified safe final state.
manual_activity: A qualified hardware operator traces and inspects every node/component/cable connection by hand and eye under approved isolation and ESD controls; the agent only organizes evidence and optional read-only health data.
required_inputs: Cable routing, bend-radius, support and clearance rules
safety_requirements: Use ESD controls, lighting and approved tools
Never force or probe connector pins
Do not connect/disconnect unsupported energized interfaces
Stop on wrong endpoint, mismatch, bent/missing pin, latch damage, strain, exposed conductor or obstruction
Preserve the found state and evidence
Do not clear logs for a mechanical check
Do not infer physical correctness from enumeration
Do not retry damaged or resistant connections without engineering inspection
agent_execution_scope: Record build, cable and endpoint identities
Prepare end-to-end checklist and evidence map
Collect operator photographs and condition notes
Correlate optional read-only post-power inventory/events after approval
Package exceptions and final state without touching hardware or deciding verdict
engineer_actions: Approve endpoint/routing map and service rules
Approve isolation, ESD, tools and operator
Perform or supervise physical trace and inspection
Stop and inspect mismatch, pin, latch or routing damage

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No SSH command can inspect pin geometry, mating depth, latch engagement, cable support or bend radius. DeepSeek's refusal is correct; physical checklist and photographs are primary evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No agent-executed mechanical command. Operator follows the approved end-to-end connection map; optional post-power inventory and health collection only corroborate continuity.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Inspection of all node/component/cable connections and the 20-minute activity remain; remote enumeration and generic log clearing cannot replace the specified physical criteria.

modernized_recommendation.status: ENDPOINT-TO-ENDPOINT MANUAL CONNECTION AND ROUTING LEDGER
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For every connection, record cable/part ID, source and destination ports, key/orientation, pin condition, seating/retention, full route, bend/support/strain, evidence and exception disposition.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns broad connection inspection into a complete traceable build-map comparison while retaining the required human visual/tactile judgment.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Inventory can show a logical device while missing partial seating, bent unused pins, wrong but electrically compatible routing or unsafe cable strain.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect mating, ESD, excessive force or routing strain can damage connectors, boards and cables; some pins/paths may require disassembly or borescope access.

project_override_considerations: Approve the exact connection population, endpoint/routing drawings, permissible live connections, pin/key inspection method, cable bend/support/clearance rules, evidence views and final-state disposition for inaccessible or damaged paths.
expected_evidence: SUT/build and node/component/cable identities plus approved endpoint/routing map
Per-connection photographs of both endpoints, pins/keying, seating/latch and full cable route
Checklist for match, orientation, retention, bend radius, support, strain, clearance and damage
Exception/stop records and safe final assembly state
Optional post-power inventory/health corroboration and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define manual inspection of connections, positioning, pins and cable routing. The needed build/routing map is an execution input, not a contradictory source rule.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical inspection and acceptance conditions are understandable. Missing map, access or safe operator would block execution, but the appropriate review classification is MANUAL ONLY.

review_improvement: Preserves DeepSeek's correct manual boundary while making every connection end-to-end traceable and adding isolation, ESD, pin, retention, routing, strain, evidence and damage-stop controls.
independent_technical_reasoning: Logical continuity is weaker than mechanical correctness: high-speed or redundant links may train with marginal seating, while a bent unused pin or excessive bend may fail later under vibration or thermal movement. Both connector ends and the intervening route must therefore be inspected and tied to an exact cable/port identity.
